title: Termwise injective K-injective complexes are fibrant in the flat model
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings on it, with abelian category $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and cochain complexes as in [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Let $I$ be a K-injective complex of $R$-modules [def-pur-kinjective-complex] each of whose terms $I^r$ is an injective object of $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let $i:A\to B$ be a morphism of complexes of $R$-modules which is a monomorphism in every degree and whose cokernel complex is acyclic [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules]. Then every morphism of complexes $f:A\to I$ extends to a morphism of complexes $g:B\to I$ with $g\circ i=f$. Consequently $I$ is a fibrant object of the flat model structure on complexes of $R$-modules of [lem-coef-sheaf-flat-model], i.e. $I\to0$ has the right lifting property against its trivial cofibrations.

proof.text: Set $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ and $C=\operatorname{coker}(i)$. The cokernel is computed degreewise: give $C^r=\operatorname{coker}(i^r)$ the differential induced by $d_B^r$; the identity $d_C^{r+1}d_C^r=0$ follows after precomposition with the epimorphism $B^r\to C^r$, and the degreewise cokernel universal property is also the cokernel universal property for chain maps. Thus $0\to A\xrightarrow{i}B\to C\to0$ is degreewise short exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact], for each $r$ the segment $H^{r-1}(C)\to H^r(A)\xrightarrow{H^r(i)}H^r(B)\to H^r(C)$ is exact. The outer terms vanish by the assumed acyclicity of $C$, so $H^r(i)$ is an isomorphism for every $r$; hence $i$ is a quasi-isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Let $Q:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ be the localization. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], $Q$ is bijective on morphisms from either $A$ or $B$ into the K-injective target $I$; its stated null-homotopy definition of K-injectivity is exactly [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Since $Q(i)$ is invertible, choose a homotopy class $[g_0]:B\to I$ mapping to $Q(f)Q(i)^{-1}$. Then $Q([g_0][i])=Q(f)$, and injectivity of $Q$ on maps from $A$ into $I$ gives $[g_0i]=[f]$. Choose a chain-map representative $g_0$ and a homotopy $h$ from $g_0i$ to $f$. By the homotopy formula of [def-pur-kinjective-complex], its components $h^r:A^r\to I^{r-1}$ satisfy
$$g_0^r i^r-f^r=d_I^{r-1}h^r+h^{r+1}d_A^r.$$

For every $r\in\mathbf Z$, the morphism $i^r:A^r\hookrightarrow B^r$ is monic and $I^{r-1}$ is injective. By the defining extension property in [def-sp-injective-resolutions], extend $h^r$ to $H^r:B^r\to I^{r-1}$ with $H^ri^r=h^r$. Choose these extensions for all degrees. Define
$$t^r=d_I^{r-1}H^r+H^{r+1}d_B^r:B^r\longrightarrow I^r.$$
There is no compatibility requirement on the choices $H^r$.

source.place: Proof of Tag 079L (lemma-characterize-K-injective): termwise injectivity permits lifting graded maps; the displayed extension is the definition of an injective object.

proof.text:
The equations $d_I^rd_I^{r-1}=0$ and $d_B^{r+1}d_B^r=0$ give
$$d_I^rt^r=d_I^rH^{r+1}d_B^r=t^{r+1}d_B^r.$$
Thus $t$ is a chain map [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Moreover, because $i$ is a chain map,
$$t^ri^r=d_I^{r-1}h^r+H^{r+1}i^{r+1}d_A^r=d_I^{r-1}h^r+h^{r+1}d_A^r=g_0^ri^r-f^r.$$
Consequently $g=g_0-t$ is a chain map $B\to I$ and $gi=f$ degreewise. This proves the extension assertion.

proof.text:
Let $j:U\to V$ be a trivial cofibration of [lem-coef-sheaf-flat-model]. Its stated cofibration and weak-equivalence classes make $j$ termwise monic and a quasi-isomorphism. Put $D=\operatorname{coker}(j)$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] to $0\to U\to V\to D\to0$ gives
$$H^r(U)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^r(V)\longrightarrow H^r(D)\longrightarrow H^{r+1}(U)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^{r+1}(V).$$
Exactness forces $H^r(D)=0$ for every $r$. The extension assertion just proved therefore extends every map $U\to I$ to $V\to I$. Every square with left arrow $j$ and right arrow $I\to0$ has this form, since the maps to zero are unique. Hence $I\to0$ has the right lifting property against all trivial cofibrations, which is fibrancy by the stated model-structure lifting axioms.
